text.p: Here are the highlights from Swiss newspapers on Friday:

- Swiss government agrees to take charge of creating humanitarian fund with banks and businesses in memory of Holocaust victims. But cabinet postpones decision on any government payment into the fund until facts are available around mid-year from a historical review of World War Two refugee policy and gold purchases from Nazi Germany.
- Swiss air force receives F/A-18 jetfighter, first of 34 to be delivered through 1999.
- Swiss National Bank says average money supply in 1996 fourth quarter rose five percent from year-earlier to 31.77 billion Swiss francs, 171 million above October forecast.

- Swiss business leaders agree to join Holocaust memorial fund demanded by world Jewish groups. Although no amount has been fixed, the agreement from banks and industry means the private sector could raise 250 million Swiss francs. The cabinet has not yet decided on a government contribution.
- Swiss Bank Corp chairman Georges Blum says Swiss National Bank should reform its operations, including switching to an interest rate policy rather than steering money supply.

- Swiss border police warn of rise in faked identity papers with new copying technologies. The number of false passports seized on a section of the border with Germany and Austria rose one-fourth in 1996 from the year before.
